payload.reason: The research was not adopted in the 1960s primarily due to a lack of funding and resources compared to superpowers like the USA and USSR, which had access to advanced computers and political support for machine translation efforts.

claims.text: The Croatian research group lacked federal funding, which hindered their ability to create a prototype for machine translation.
Unlike their counterparts in the USA and USSR, the Croatian researchers had to work without an actual computer, limiting their results to theoretical work.
The political context of the time prioritized military applications of computational linguistics, which the Croatian group could not compete with due to their limited resources.
